smell: Four YAML engines in the tree: sigs.k8s.io/yaml (direct), go.yaml.in/yaml/v2 (via k8s), go.yaml.in/yaml/v3 (via cobra/doc + kube-openapi), gopkg.in/yaml.v3 (via go-proxmox + testify + charm/log). Binary ships N engines even though only sigs.k8s.io/yaml is directly imported. The go.yaml.in/v2 vs gopkg.in/yaml.v3 split is especially suspicious — go.yaml.in is a fork with sparse upstream tracking.
evidence:
# go mod graph | grep yaml
github.com/qxtaiba/okdctl go.yaml.in/yaml/v2@v2.4.3
github.com/qxtaiba/okdctl go.yaml.in/yaml/v3@v3.0.4
github.com/qxtaiba/okdctl sigs.k8s.io/yaml@v1.6.0
charm.land/log/v2 gopkg.in/yaml.v3@v3.0.1
github.com/luthermonson/go-proxmox gopkg.in/yaml.v3@v3.0.1
fix_summary: Document the split in a deps policy section in CLAUDE.md: sigs.k8s.io/yaml is REQUIRED for k8s Secret marshaling (JSON-tag respect); the three transitive engines are pulled by upstream deps we can't control (k8s, cobra, testify). No action on the code; action is on documentation so future PRs don't accidentally try to 'consolidate' and break the k8s addon path. See seam #10 — modernization owns 'drop dep X in favor of stdlib', this finding is a policy note only.

smell: go.yaml.in/yaml/v2 and go.yaml.in/yaml/v3 are a vanity-domain fork of the original gopkg.in/yaml.v{2,3}. The domain (go.yaml.in) is a 2024+ rehosting that the k8s/cobra ecosystems migrated to after gopkg.in archived yaml.v2. Pulled transitively by k8s.io/api, k8s.io/apimachinery, cobra/doc. Both versions are in tree simultaneously — v2.4.3 AND v3.0.4. Provenance is upstream-controlled but worth acknowledging: we do NOT control which YAML parser validates k8s manifests we build.
evidence:
go.yaml.in/yaml/v2 v2.4.3 // indirect
go.yaml.in/yaml/v3 v3.0.4 // indirect
fix_summary: Acceptance note only. The go.yaml.in move is the same maintainer collective as gopkg.in (kubernetes-sigs). No action available — k8s.io/api and spf13/cobra force the floor. If okdctl ever directly imports go.yaml.in/yaml/v3 (instead of going through sigs.k8s.io/yaml), revisit.
rule_source: SKILL.md §1 cluster 1 license-compat and §3 Agent A maintenance signal

smell: github.com/luthermonson/go-proxmox v0.4.1 is the ONLY API path to Proxmox VE — used for node/storage/bridge discovery in the wizard. Pinned at v0.4.1 (2026-04-03, fresh), but the v0.x major means the API is 'unstable by convention' per semver. One upstream breaking release would force a wizard refactor on our schedule, not theirs. Additionally: go-proxmox has ONE active maintainer (luthermonson) → bus factor 1. Mitigations worth documenting: (a) proxmox_discovery.go is the only consumer, (b) the types we consume (Node, Storage, Bridge) are derived from the Proxmox /api2/json schema which IS stable.
fix_summary: Document in CLAUDE.md §dependencies (new section): 'go-proxmox is pinned at v0.x; treat every minor bump as a breaking-change review. The Proxmox API call surface used is isolated to internal/tui/wizard/steps/proxmox_discovery.go — breakage limits to the Proxmox discovery wizard step, not the deploy path.' Additionally, maintain a fallback: if go-proxmox becomes unmaintained, the call surface (Node/Storage/Network listing) is small enough to reimplement against the raw /api2/json endpoints (~200 LOC). Flag for RFC review if upstream goes silent >6mo.
severity_reason: rubric §4/ad-hoc: v0.x single-maintainer dep on the critical discovery path is not a blocker today (fresh release + isolated call surface) but deserves the 'should fix within 2 releases' tier — the fix is a documented abandonment plan, not code.
rule_source: Go semver convention: v0.y.z is pre-stable

smell: github.com/gorilla/websocket v1.4.2 (2020-03-19) pulled transitively by go-proxmox. gorilla/websocket is in MAINTENANCE mode — gorilla toolkit was archived 2022, un-archived 2023 under new maintainers. Current recommended WS lib is coder/websocket or nhooyr.io/websocket (same author, renamed). Five-year-old release on a security-sensitive surface (TLS, framing). govulncheck catches known CVEs, but pin-by-call-graph is our only defense against unpublished ones.
fix_summary: Out of our control (transitive, pulled by go-proxmox). Document: 'WebSocket transport for Proxmox shell/console lives in a dep we don't call — internal/tui/wizard/steps/proxmox_discovery.go only uses REST APIs. If a WS CVE lands, the import is not reached.' Verify go mod why -m github.com/gorilla/websocket doesn't reach a called site. If go-proxmox upstream drops gorilla in a future release, take the bump.

smell: github.com/charmbracelet/ultraviolet v0.0.0-20260416155717-489999b90468 is pinned to a pseudo-version (commit SHA, not a tagged release). The version string encodes a commit hash — but the project has never tagged a release, so this is de-facto HEAD tracking of an unreleased library. The same project is pulled by four different charm.land deps at three different pseudo-versions (bubbles uses 20260205, lipgloss+log use 20251205, bubbletea + main require use 20260416). MVS picks the newest. This is how the charm ecosystem works today — but the exposure is: no stable-API contract, zero release notes, zero changelog between bumps.
fix_summary: Acceptance note. Charm ecosystem convention is that ultraviolet (the internal renderer) is not publicly-tagged. Treat every charm.land/* bump as an implicit ultraviolet bump and test the wizard end-to-end (internal/tui/wizard/** is already excluded from most audits — this is precisely why). No action on the pin itself; document the convention and schedule quarterly 'bump charm.land libs' in roadmap.md so drift is visible.
rule_source: CLAUDE.md §architecture-notes: charm libs intentional UI stack

smell: golang.org/x/exp pinned at v0.0.0-20231006140011 (Oct 2023) — almost 2.5 years old. The module has newer versions available (v0.0.0-20250620... in module cache). Pulled transitively by charm.land/log/v2, which only imports golang.org/x/exp/slog (a BACKPORT of log/slog that the stdlib now provides since Go 1.21 — and this repo targets 1.25 per go.mod). charm.land/log/v2's go.mod still requires x/exp for the slog path. Go 1.25 makes x/exp/slog entirely redundant for us — but we can't fix it; charm.land/log/v2 requires the old pin.
fix_summary: File upstream issue at github.com/charmbracelet/log requesting a drop of the x/exp/slog import in favor of stdlib log/slog. Until that lands, the stale pin persists. Alternative: add an explicit 'require golang.org/x/exp <newer>' in our go.mod to force a bump — but this is fighting MVS for no real gain since we don't directly import x/exp. Seam #10: modernization owns the 'drop x/exp in favor of stdlib' fix, but the fix sits in a DEPENDENCY not our code — so it's truly neither skill's action.

smell: License compatibility audit: NO copyleft (GPL/AGPL/LGPL) or custom/unclear licenses in the transitive dep tree. All 36 deps (direct + indirect) carry permissive licenses: MIT (charm.land/*, cobra, diskfs, cbor, godotenv, progressbar, copier, godotenv, godotenv, md2man, and friends), Apache-2.0 (k8s.io/*, cobra, go-proxmox, klog, logr, magefile, go.yaml.in/*), BSD-3 (blackfriday, gorilla/websocket, googleapis, golang.org/x/*, asciiset). No action required — static-link + goreleaser + apt/rpm/homebrew distribution is clean. This is a verified-clean finding recorded for the audit trail, not an actionable defect.
fix_summary: Record the audit baseline in CLAUDE.md §credentials-and-secrets (or a new §dependencies): 'All runtime deps are MIT/Apache-2.0/BSD-3. Never add a GPL/AGPL/LGPL dep without an RFC.' This is a tripwire for future PRs. No code change.

smell: Pin hygiene audit: GitHub Actions in every workflow file are pinned by full 40-char SHA with the version tag in a trailing comment. Every usage of actions/checkout, actions/setup-go, golangci/golangci-lint-action, github/codeql-action, goreleaser/goreleaser-action, sigstore/cosign-installer, anchore/sbom-action, hashicorp/setup-terraform, EndBug/label-sync, actions/labeler, slsa-framework/slsa-github-generator is SHA-pinned. This is best-in-class supply-chain hygiene. No floating tag refs anywhere in .github/workflows/. Recorded as a positive finding for the audit trail.
evidence:
// .github/workflows/ci.yml:L15-19
- uses: actions/checkout@de0fac2e4500dabe0009e67214ff5f5447ce83dd # v6
- uses: actions/setup-go@4a3601121dd01d1626a1e23e37211e3254c1c06c # v6
- uses: golangci/golangci-lint-action@1e7e51e771db61008b38414a730f564565cf7c20 # v9
fix_summary: Optional: add a CI guard that fails if any workflow introduces a non-SHA action ref. Example — a lightweight rule in a new lint job running a regex over .github/workflows/ that flags uses: org/name@tag (where tag is not 40 hex). This defends the hygiene against drift over time. See pinact (github.com/suzuki-shunsuke/pinact) for a ready-made tool.

smell: Makefile 'lint' target installs golangci-lint with @latest — non-reproducible. Same pattern in the CI workflow (golangci-lint-action version: latest) and in the 'security' CI job (govulncheck@latest) and 'lint-yaml' (yamlfmt@latest). A local make lint run next month will pick up a different linter version than today, which can mean new findings or new false-positives without a code change. The go-based tooling is installed at 'latest' even though Go has first-class version pinning via go tool / go run.
fix_summary: Pin golangci-lint and govulncheck in the Makefile and CI. Three options: (a) bump to Go 1.24+ 'tools' directive in go.mod so `go tool` manages versions (cleanest); (b) create a tools/tools.go with blank imports and run `go install golang.org/x/vuln/cmd/govulncheck@v1.1.4` (explicit); (c) for CI, set `version: v2.x.y` on golangci/golangci-lint-action instead of `latest` — removes action-side drift while still letting local make-lint float. Recommend option (a). Impact: reproducible local lint runs.
rule_source: SKILL.md §2 Makefile if present for tool pins

smell: goreleaser-action is SHA-pinned (good), but the version parameter it resolves IS a tag, not a SHA — version: v2.15.2 in both release.yml and release-prep.yml. This is the goreleaser CLI binary version, not the GH Action. The action downloads the goreleaser CLI from GitHub releases at runtime. If goreleaser releases were ever re-tagged (a malicious force-push to a tag), we'd pull a different binary. Acceptable trade-off because (a) goreleaser is a widely-used project, (b) its releases are cosigned, but worth noting.
evidence:
// .github/workflows/release.yml:25-29
- uses: goreleaser/goreleaser-action@e24998b8b67b290c2fa8b7c14fcfa7de2c5c9b8c # v7
  id: goreleaser
  with:
    version: "v2.15.2"
fix_summary: Minor tightening: if goreleaser publishes binary SHA256s (it does, as part of its own release process), add a post-install `sha256sum goreleaser` step and match against a pinned hash. Alternatively, accept the v2.15.2 tag trust model — goreleaser signs its own releases with cosign. No urgent action.

smell: validate-terraform job uses terraform_version: "1.10" — a minor-floor pin ('latest 1.10.x'). This is neither fully pinned (a specific 1.10.3) nor explicitly floor-only. Terraform minor bumps can change provider behavior subtly. For a module that drives destructive infra (proxmox-okd), the CI validation running on different 1.10.z each week is a reproducibility smell.
fix_summary: Pin to full semver: terraform_version: "1.10.3" (or whatever is current), and bump explicitly in a PR when you want the new version. Alternative: add a .terraform-version file in infrastructure/terraform/ that documents the pin as a first-class artifact (tfenv / tfswitch convention). Seam: iac audit may also flag this — defer to iac findings if they exist.
rule_source: Terraform docs: pin CI versions for reproducibility

smell: github.com/schollz/progressbar/v3 v3.19.0 is used at a single call site (internal/download/download.go:16) to render one progress bar for ISO download. It pulls gopkg.in/yaml.v3 (test), github.com/mitchellh/colorstring (2019 release — stale), github.com/rivo/uniseg, github.com/mattn/go-runewidth, github.com/chengxilo/virtualterm. Given the project ALREADY has lipgloss/bubbletea (charm.land ecosystem) for terminal rendering, maintaining a separate progress-bar lib creates a second terminal-width-computation codepath. The mitchellh/colorstring dep is 6 years stale.
fix_summary: Replace schollz/progressbar/v3 with charm.land/bubbles/v2/progress or a 30-line hand-rolled bar using lipgloss + runewidth (already in tree via charm deps). Drops 5 transitive deps, removes stale mitchellh/colorstring, unifies terminal-rendering on the charm stack. Risk is medium because the current bar is battle-tested for the download UX — reimplementing means re-doing SIGWINCH handling, TTY-vs-pipe detection, and the 'don't render when progressBars=false' gate that tui.ProgressBarsEnabled already provides. Plan before swap.
rule_source: CLAUDE.md §architecture-notes: charm libs are intentional UI stack

smell: CLAUDE.md has sections for commit-messages, code-comments, architecture-notes, tooling, credentials-and-secrets — but NO dependencies policy section. No documented rule for: (a) which licenses are allowed for new direct deps, (b) whether v0.x deps require an RFC, (c) pin-by-SHA expectations for new workflow actions, (d) the 'charm libs stay' carve-out that this audit's SKILL.md already enforces but only there. A new contributor adding a GPL dep has nothing in the repo instructions that forbids it.
fix_summary: Add a §Dependencies section to CLAUDE.md with: (1) 'Only MIT/Apache-2.0/BSD-{2,3}/ISC licenses for runtime deps; GPL/AGPL/LGPL requires RFC and is de facto blocked for the shipped binary.' (2) 'v0.x deps: acceptable only for isolated call surfaces — document the fallback plan in the dep's adjacent comment.' (3) 'GitHub Actions MUST pin by 40-char SHA with a version comment trailer.' (4) 'Tool pins (Makefile, CI installs) use `go install pkg@vX.Y.Z` or the go.mod tools directive — never @latest.' This turns SKILL.md conventions into enforceable repo policy.
rule_source: SKILL.md §4 grounding: 'CLAUDE.md does not specify deps policy; flag one as suggestion'
